A1.justification: Both complete 35-page PDFs describe the same PID Steering work. Text and visual inspection support comparison of all sections, equations, tables and figures. Appendices A–C, on pages 16–35, have identical text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: V2 reports original toxicity-mitigation, jailbreaking and image-steering experiments, controller ablations and additional appendix results.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and outcomes, including Tables 1–3 and the main-text and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The PID steering rule, its proportional/integral/derivative components, and sequential and non-sequential constructions remain unchanged in Section 3, Definition 1 and Equations 16–18.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same toxicity, jailbreaking, general-language and COCO-caption image-style tasks. The deeper-safety-aligned Gemma scenario in Appendix C.2 and Table 3 is already present in v2.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: ActADD, CAA, AURA, ITI-C and the AcT variants for toxicity; DIM, ITI and RePE for jailbreaking; and Mean-AcT for image steering. The revised Turner citation does not introduce a different baseline.

E3.justification: The reported settings remain identical, including 1,000 toxicity prompts, the AdvBench 80/20 split, 512 harmless Alpaca samples, and 2,048 training/512 validation COCO prompts. Models, metrics, intervention procedures and gain sweeps are retained.

E4.justification: The controller-dynamics demonstrations, Figure 6 gain ablations, Appendix C.3 stability-interval analysis and qualitative image examples are unchanged. Moving Figure 4 does not add an analysis.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains averaging over 10 runs and the same uncertainty reporting. Neither the main text nor appendices change repeated-run information or statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: All numerical tables and graphical results match. For example, Table 1 retains PID-AcT classifier toxicity of 0.51 ± 0.21 for Gemma2-2B and 0.72 ± 0.49 for Llama3-8B; Table 3 retains PID ASR of 34.75 for deeper-safety-aligned Gemma.

T1.justification: The definitions, discretization lemma, stability propositions and overshoot theorems are unchanged. Appendix B, including its proofs and nonlinear-remainder analysis, is identical; main-text page breaks do not revise the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: interpreting existing steering as P-control, introducing PID Steering, reducing steady-state error and overshoot, and improving behavioral control while preserving utility.

C2.justification: Interpretations of controller gains and style-versus-content tradeoffs are retained. Both versions acknowledge that the stability-first, one-gain-at-a-time strategy may miss optimal gains and broader feasible regions; Appendix C.3 retains its lack-of-optimality-theorem qualification.

D1.justification: The public-code statement, supplementary-code disclosure, reproducibility statement and documented experimental details are unchanged. No implementation, hardware, hyperparameter or access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The revised Turner entry identifies the same arXiv:2308.10248 already cited in v2. Its author/title/year changes are bibliographic metadata revisions, not new related work. Appendix A and the paper's research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 revises one Turner bibliography entry's authors, title and year, with corresponding 2024a/2024b citation labels. The scientific prose, explanations and section order otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 moves from page 9 to page 10 beside Figure 5. Spacing and pagination change throughout the main text and references, including page splits in Definition 1 and the conclusion. Figure/table contents and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the duplicated Turner reference internally consistent and groups Figures 4–5, but retains the duplicate entry and introduces less continuous pagination for Definition 1 and the conclusion. These limited editorial tradeoffs leave overall quality essentially stable; the method, proofs, empirical evidence, interpretations and reproducibility information are unchanged.
